Playing the Sims is great, it's a childhood classic, brings me back to when I first entered the world of PC games.

It gets depressing around 4am when I realise I've been playing for hours on end, sat by myself, playing the life of someone who is more successful, funnier, more attractive, wealthier and generally better off than me, living in my dream house. I don't want a big house, nothing fancy - I don't like the idea of having to do a lot of extra cleaning. But having a spare room and maybe a small pond would be nice. My sims always have so much space for an allotment. In this economy, how are you meant to have an allotment? It's ridiculous. Plus my sims usually have at least 8 friends. I can only aspire to that.

Recommended now that the base game includes toddlers, and obviously much better if you have the expansions packs too. What Sims 4 lacks in personality (which Sims 2 definitely had) and open-world creativity (Sims 3) it makes up for in other ways, especially if gameplay-enhancing mods are added to make it more realistic and the sims a bit more "human". For me though I particularly enjoy the building mechanics. Also I've had no corruption issues that I experienced in my Sims 2 game (broken memories in Sims 2 often caused this). I also like the fact you can share sims and lots with others via the Gallery. So I guess I'm (just about) in the "fan" camp, although I do find the fact you can't create your own unique World (as you could in Sims 3) pretty restricting.

The game itself is bare-bones, although free at the point of writing this. I cannot recommend it by any means for as long as Sims 1, 2 and 3 exist; they stripped down the best elements of each game (esp. Sims 3), and then launched an "empty" game of sorts. This is only to spoon-feed you content at a pace for a ridiculous amount of money you'd need to pay if you ever wanted to have the FULL experience, and it stinks of that infamous mobile gaming, FOMO effect.

So, you might wonder. With about 260 hours of play, how come I don't recommend it? The answer is simple.

The fun and joy I'm having with this game is all credited to some 15.000 mods installed, and to those wonderful creative people who made them all possible. Cheers!

I started playing The Sims with the very first game and have played every part since then. Watching the series grow over the years has been amazing. Each new game brought improvements, better graphics, and new features that made the experience even more enjoyable.
Even just creating Sims is already a lot of fun. You can spend hours designing characters, building houses, and creating your own little worlds without even needing to play through the actual game.

The classic cheat codes also make it easier to play the way you want, and the ability to add mods brings even more possibilities with new outfits, furniture, and countless other additions.

I’ve spent so many hours with The Sims over the years, especially back when I played a lot through Origin, and it’s a game that will always have a special place in my heart. ♥
I really hope I can find the time again someday to fully sink into it like I used to and create new stories and worlds...

I used to enjoy playing The Sims 4, but EA’s recent decisions finally pushed me away from the game.

The Sims community has always been carried by custom content creators. They make the hair, clothes, furniture, and mods that keep the game interesting long after release. Players could support those creators directly through platforms like Patreon or their own websites. It worked perfectly fine.

Now EA is introducing a marketplace and inserting itself as the middleman. From what’s being said, creators only receive around 30% while EA takes the rest. So EA gets the majority of the money for content they didn’t even make.

Why exactly do we need this marketplace when players could already support creators directly?

It doesn’t help creators. It doesn’t help players. It just gives EA another way to monetize a community that was already doing fine on its own.

I enjoyed the game for what it was, but this level of greed is exhausting. Because of decisions like this, I’m done with The Sims 4.

There's one thing that irked me a bit in this title. Lots. In sims 3 you could freely place empty lots wherever you want, and choose a size. In sims 4 every town has preset lots, you can't edit their size. 64x64 lots are not present in the base game.

Although I bought this for 88% off I am very much underwhelmed.
First the good. The building mechanics are pretty good, best I've seen in the Sims.
Now the bad. The only added feature to game play from the Sims 3 is that sims can have moods (inspired, sad, flirty, etc.) and that can influence interactions and sim status (the color of the gem over their head). The customized style options for clothing, furniture and floors from the Sims 3 have been downgraded to pre-made options and no ability to actually make a custom color outfit (if you want a jacket in red but the jacket does not have red in it's pre-made swatches you're not getting it in red). Sims' traits have been "simplified" to fit the new mood aspect of the game. Things to do in the game world are limited (there is a gym, a museum, a bar, and a park in every "world"). Interactions with other sims is weird, my characters apparently don't like to look at the person their talking to and my sim will just decide they don't want to do what I tell them to do.
Overall, get the Sims 3, the expansion packs offer more content and exploring the neighborhood can actually be fun.
